shared_elements: frontal human face with eyes, nose and mouth at the top
faint indication of arms/hands on the torso
museum display on a low plinth
justification: Both are frontal anthropomorphic stone monoliths in which a broad flat face occupies the upper block and a tapering, legless columnar body carries vestigial arms across the torso, so the basic compositional scheme corresponds closely. The decisive difference is finish and content: A carries a dense programme of low-relief motifs (headdress bands, disc, chevron belt, ornaments) on a smoothed surface, whereas B is a coarse, almost unmodelled boulder with only the crudest facial features and no ornament at all.
